as_told.title: Wreck of the Titan foretold the Titanic

plain: A novel written in 1898, years before the Titanic sank, seems to tell its story ahead of time. In Morgan Robertson's Futility, or the Wreck of the Titan, the Titan is the largest and most luxurious ocean liner ever built, and it hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic on an April night and sinks. Michels tells it several times as something he knows from his reading. Once he dates the book only vaguely, to the early twentieth century, about ten years before the Titanic, and another time he says "like 12 years before". The writer Eric Wargo also tells it, drawing on his own book Time Loops, which is about dreams and hunches that seem to foresee the future. If it is more than coincidence, it would suggest that people can glimpse what is still to come.
